name: Accordion
description: A vertically stacked set of interactive headings that each reveal a section of content. Can operate in single (only one item open) or multiple (multiple items open) mode.
usage: Wrap `AccordionItem` components within the main `Accordion` component.
Each `AccordionItem` must contain an `AccordionTrigger` and an `AccordionContent`.
Set `type="multiple"` on `Accordion` to allow multiple items open simultaneously.
Control the open state using `value` (controlled) or `defaultValue` (uncontrolled) props on `Accordion`.
The `value` or `defaultValue` for `type="single"` is a string corresponding to the `value` prop of the `AccordionItem`.
The `value` or `defaultValue` for `type="multiple"` is an array of strings.
Use the `textSize` prop on `AccordionTrigger` to adjust the trigger text size ('xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg').
Set `disabled={true}` on `AccordionItem` to disable a specific item.
examples:
```tsx
// Single Type (Default)
import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent } from '@levain/ui-react';

<Accordion type="single" defaultValue="item-1" className="w-full">
  <AccordionItem value="item-1">
    <AccordionTrigger>Is it accessible?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>
      Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="item-2">
    <AccordionTrigger textSize="lg">Is it styled?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>
      Yes. It comes with default styles that matches the design system.
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```
design: Use `type="single"` when users only need to see one section of content at a time (e.g., FAQs).
Use `type="multiple"` when users might need to compare or reference information across different sections.
Keep trigger text concise and descriptive of the content within.
Ensure content within `AccordionContent` is clearly related to its trigger.
Use appropriate `textSize` on the trigger for the context.
accessibility: Follows the WAI-ARIA Accordion design pattern.
`AccordionTrigger` renders as a `<button>` inside an `<h3>` by default, providing semantic structure.
Correct ARIA attributes (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-disabled`) are automatically applied.
Focus is managed correctly when interacting with triggers.
Ensure sufficient contrast for text and focus indicators.

props.name: type
props.description: Determines whether one or multiple items can be opened simultaneously.

props.name: value
props.description: The controlled value (item value or array of item values) of the accordion item(s) to be opened.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The uncontrolled default value (item value or array of item values) of the accordion item(s) to be opened.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Event handler called when the expanded state changes. Receives `string | undefined` for single type, `string[]` for multiple type.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes for the root accordion div.

subcomponents.name: AccordionItem
subcomponents.description: Container for an individual accordion section.

props.name: value
props.description: A unique value for the accordion item, used to control its state.

props.name: disabled
props.description: When true, prevents the user from interacting with the item.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes for the accordion item div.

subcomponents.name: AccordionTrigger
subcomponents.description: The button element that toggles the accordion item's content.

props.name: textSize
props.description: Size of the text within the trigger button.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes for the trigger button.

subcomponents.name: AccordionContent
subcomponents.description: The container for the content revealed when the item is open.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes for the content div.
